domainRule: The full initial warning follows the frozen cinematic. Burst navigation asks for continuous travel and one signalled reversal, with a brief visible hold while an earlier body passes; being outside one preview does not finish a burst. The final three-way attack accepts either safe side and holds there until all bodies pass. Every individual shot has a matching visible line, locks .60 seconds before launch and never retargets. Preview lines and cleared trails never damage. Every actual body contact is fatal despite HP, E guard, dodge or R protection; R cinematics pause but cannot erase active takeovers.
bladeReactionMethod: 180 actual-step walks: both characters, three layouts and their mirrors, five player starts and three boss starts; .35-second input reaction after initial/relocation cues and the final diagonal turn. No dash, buff, attack, teleport, HP edit or invulnerability. 180 additional still/one-direction/circle policies test whether simple camping solves the sequence. The full challenge bots separately use .53/.29/.14-second reaction policies and ten-Hz decisions.
pursuitReactionMethod: 108 actual walks cover both fixed characters, both boss phases, nine arena starts and three boss positions. They delay .35 seconds on initial preparation, outbound, reversal, crossing and final tracking/lock cues. Repeated with .65 seconds, with and without a real Space dash once per phase.180 stationary/eight-fixed-direction/circle controls and18 first-burst-only controls test simple policies. Full challenges use their original .53/.29/.14 reaction policies at10Hz, including navigation changes; motors release at already observed targets at60Hz, never erase collision or damage. Burst movement is not stopped merely because one old preview has been escaped. Each isolated result includes all actual launch times; complete full-run samples are included separately. No teleport, HP edit or invulnerability override in these traversals. Medians include3/3.2/3.4/3.6/3.8-second entry cinematics, during which combat/cooldowns freeze.
scoreRule: Actual HP damage × combo multiplier + 60 per landed JUST attack + 150 per JUST dodge. No overkill or clear bonus. Combo +0.25 per 8 hits (max 2.5), FEVER adds 0.5 (max 3).
takeoverRouteMethod: 40 actual-step walks from center and four corners across both characters; dodge cooldown stays unavailable. Eight additional tests start at the initial guide and remain still. No attack, HP override, invulnerability or teleport during traversal.
openingReactionMethod: Each new normal attack from a fixed open-arena position: stand still versus walk upward after 0.35 seconds, both fixed characters. No dodge or skill, no HP or damage override; initial spawn invulnerability is explicitly removed for this collider test.
purpleReactionMethod: Separate single-Purple open-arena scenarios: walk upward after the stated delay from the lock cue. No dodge or skills. These measure timing at one position, not human success rates.
limitations: Input controllers know visible hazard geometry, numbered light goals and the marked real silhouette; their win rates are not human win rates. The audition policy has a profile-dependent chance of choosing the visibly wrong figure.

Controllers use visible geometry and stop attacking during takeovers. New relocation warnings, the final diagonal turn, and pursuit tracking/lock transitions incur their profile reaction delay; initial warnings also require elapsed reaction time. These are geometry-aware policies, not calibrated human skill levels.
Profile differences are policies, not a calibrated human skill ordering; a middle policy can fare worse than a slower policy in some character matchups.
Victory and boss timing medians include completed fights only.
The 300-second simulation guard is a test safety measure; there is no time limit in the game.
Historical booth-balance-report.json measures the superseded timed mode and is not validation of this untimed challenge.
method: Actual v19 untimed five-boss challenge, fixed standard difficulty and engine seed424242. Both fixed characters use real QWER, movement, collision and cooldowns at60Hz; +65HP after nonfinal bosses, victory after the fifth. No HP/damage override, projectile deletion, teleport or game timeout. The offline300s safety guard is reported separately.
difficultyRevision: Max joins between If and Moving as a camera/film audition examiner. The original four bosses retain their HP, attack values, QWER interactions and seven-pattern rotations. Seven pattern options retain every previous skill. Five-cast rotations retain the original takeover slots and cadence. Only the opening slot cycles personality attack6, previous concept attack5 and original attack0; all seven skills appear within11 scheduled casts. After Moving completes his first takeover and its earned counter window, HP at or below45percent prioritizes the second takeover at the next clear attack boundary, retaining the next normal skill and all warning geometry. Pino throws three staggered red-capped bottles and Daegil pursues with two committed charges, unchanged mechanically. If reserves five recent positions and fires five frame shots; Moving chains five alternating dashes with delayed trail cuts. Max uses two/three camera flashes, seven staggered photos, six returning photos in two groups, and one/three moving frames; every lock/return warning remains visible. Existing takeovers remain intact. PlayerHP260 and postcast recovery factor0.90 remain unchanged from v18; all existing boss HP, heal65, player QWER, damage and warning timings are unchanged. Max uses5200 rankedHP and41 base damage.
variantRouteMethod: 216 real walks: three bosses × both characters × both phases × two cast parities × nine arena starts. React .35s after each publicly visible phase cue; walk only, no dash, buff, attack, HP edit or teleport during traversal.216 still/fixed-direction controls use the same fixtures. The phase/parity matrix deliberately checks both selection paths for each variant.
newNormalMethod: 240 actual index5 casts: four bosses × two characters × two phases × center/four corners × geometry-aware walking/still/up-only policies. The isolated walker waits .35s after each individual fixed warning, then walks outside the already-visible fixed preview geometry. Rapid subsequent warnings have independent reaction clocks. It does not approach the boss, attack, dodge, buff, edit HP or delete projectiles; no future spawn/hidden aim data is read. This strict cue-response fixture is separate from the attacking campaign controller.
difficultyOrderMethod: Independent ranked-equivalent duels start each boss at the same fresh player resources under the same controller policies. Their damage and clear rates are reported separately from campaign reach/conditional clear rates, so early deaths do not hide later-boss exposure. Clear-time alone is not a difficulty ranking.
controllerRevision: Retains .53/.29/.14 profile delays, ten-Hz decisions and60Hz release at already-observed targets. Projected risk from visible current projectiles remains reaction-delayed. Public personality escape targets are read only after an individual fixed-cue delay; Q is released while moving to that target. These geometry-aware input policies are not calibrated human skill levels, and paired before/after engine runs use this identical updated controller separately.

baselineComparison.method: Paired standard challenge runs, fixed engine seed424242, identical current input controller across both engines, three policies x two roles x30 seeds. No state edits after createGame; offline300s guard only. The old four-boss version and new five-boss version are not the same-length challenge, so compare whole-run figures as resource/duration change only. First-two-boss prefix snapshots isolate the preserved shared opening; later If/Max/Moving are intentionally strengthened.
limitations: Geometry-aware policies are not human win rates or calibrated skill tiers.
Added fifth fight makes aggregate wins and timing incomparable as a pure boss-difficulty measure.
The same current public helper functions are used for both old/new state schemas; absent Max state never enters the Max branch.
baselineComparison.interpretation: The five-boss campaign adds one complete fight, so total completion rates and victory times are not a pure difficulty comparison. All180 paired runs have identical first-two-boss prefix snapshots (including both unreached prefixes). The fresh-resource duels below compare the bosses independently.
